page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the c3 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, a 105 MB L3 cache, and 16 GB of system memory, yielding 4 GB of RAM per core. This instance is bundled with 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed local disk access, while containing zero GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance split between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU scoring 1617.89 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1714.0, both placing in the middle 50% tier. Conversely, multi-core and memory-bound metrics fall into lower tiers. The multi-core Geekbench score of 3812.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 3323.04 are in the bottom 25%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 10% at 21.7 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 29.2 GB/sec and 22.26 GB/sec respectively, placing memory performance in the bottom 25%.

The inclusion of a 402 GB local NVMe SSD provides a high-speed storage tier directly attached to the instance, which offsets the lower memory bandwidth for disk-heavy operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the instance offers a balanced resource density for workloads that require dedicated compute cores and fast local storage without needing massive memory arrays. However, the weak multi-core scaling and lower memory throughput present a tradeoff for highly parallelized compute tasks. This server is suited for workloads such as static web serving, single-threaded text and data processing, and lightweight database operations that benefit from local SSD storage.
